page: Amazon Web Services m6g.2xlarge is a general-purpose server powered by an AWS Graviton processor. It features 8 physical cores and 8 virtual CPUs based on the ARMv8 arm64 architecture, utilizing the AWS Neoverse-N1 model running at 2.5 GHz. The processor provides a dedicated CPU allocation with 1 thread per core, supported by 64 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. The system is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding 4.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or a GPU, and operates on the Nitro hypervisor with a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks place the m6g.2xlarge in the average tier for several multi-core and memory-bound operations. The stress-ng multi-core CPU test scored 12135.21, and the Geekbench multi-core score reached 5355.0, both falling within the average range. Memory bandwidth tests show 472.85 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 120.79 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. However, single-core performance is weaker, with a Geekbench single-core score of 936.0 and a Passmark CPU score of 5218.9. Tradeoffs are evident in single-threaded compression and decompression, where gzip compression at 20.34 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 7.3 GB/sec register as weak and poor respectively. Cryptographic and vector instruction sets are limited, with no AVX or AMX support, though AES cryptography is supported.

The server demonstrates average performance in database operations, with a Passmark database score of 5174.5 and Redis SET operations reaching 9.56 million operations per second. Static web serving throughput is also average at 9.38 GB/sec. Conversely, LLM inference speeds are weak to poor, with text generation on a small 135M model yielding 35.33 tokens per second. Given the ARM-based architecture and dedicated physical cores, this instance offers resource density and qualitative cost efficiency for multi-threaded general-purpose workloads, such as web serving, database operations, and software compilation, while being less suitable for single-threaded tasks or heavy vector-based computations.
